rules.rule: The skill is discoverable and its description says when to use it
Each abstraction's preconditions, postconditions, invariants and observable behavior are defined before classes are created
The contract specifies valid inputs, expected outputs and error handling, and describes behavior rather than implementation details

assertions.value: valid inputs, expected outputs,\s+and error-handling behavior

rules.rule: Implementations never strengthen preconditions to reject inputs the base contract accepts

assertions.value: rejects?\s+inputs accepted by the base contract

rules.rule: Implementations never weaken postconditions and preserve invariants and observable behavior
Implementations handle errors and exceptional conditions consistently with the declared contract

assertions.value: errors and exceptional conditions\s+consistently with the declared contract

rules.rule: Inheritance is used only for genuine behavioral subtypes; interfaces when several implementations honor one contract

assertions.value: inheritance only when the subtype\s+genuinely satisfies
interfaces when multiple implementations\s+can honor the same contract

rules.rule: Composition is preferred over inheritance when behavioral expectations are incompatible; inheritance is never chosen for code reuse alone
Consumers never have to inspect concrete types to know whether an operation is supported
Hierarchies do not force unrelated behaviors together, overrides keep the meaning of inherited operations, and restricted operations have explicit contracts

assertions.value: explicit contracts for operations that may fail

rules.rule: The workflow runs Analyze, Define, Evaluate, Design, Validate, Implement in that order, with implementation last

assertions.value: only after validating the design against LSP

rules.rule: No inheritance hierarchy is created before its behavioral contract, and inheritance is never used merely to share code

assertions.value: Do not create inheritance hierarchies before defining their\s+behavioral contracts
Do not use inheritance merely to share code

rules.rule: No unsupported assumptions about implementation behavior are introduced and the established architecture and business rules are preserved

assertions.value: Preserve the established project architecture and business\s+rules

rules.rule: Before classes are created the five deliverables are provided: contracts, guarantees and invariants, implementation compatibility, substitutability risks, and the inheritance/interface/composition justification

assertions.value: 2\. [^\n]*guarantees and invariants consumers can rely on

rules.rule: The definition of done requires every implementation to honor its contract with no implementation-specific consumer workarounds
The skill stays LSP-only: other SOLID principles and implementing code before validation are out of scope
The skill ships a README.md and a Rules table covering exactly the spec IDs
A subtype that throws on an operation its base type supports is flagged as an LSP violation and redesigned before any code is written
A request to inherit purely to reuse code with incompatible behavior is redirected to composition with a justification
